articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
Chinese technology firms are bracing for impacts on their ambitious artificial intelligence plans as the U.S. tightens restrictions on China 's access to the world's cutting-edge chips.
Chinese tech giant Alibaba , which on Thursday announced another quarter of strong revenue growth for its global AI cloud and compute services, warned that the new U.S. rules could affect some of its global data center expansion plans. It said it was still assessing the repercussions.
The Trump administration this week issued new rules in the wake of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation, following the news that he’d had an extramarital affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy.
The rules now restrict remote computing access through data centers in third countries, the latest U.S. move to curtail China’s abilities to use advanced Nvidia chips to train its increasingly capable AI models.
Alibaba's AI revenues are surging as demand grows
As the technology race between the two superpowers intensifies, existing U.S. export restrictions already barred China from getting the world’s most powerful chips.
But some Chinese companies have been able to bypass those restrictions by renting remote computing access to train AI models, pushing the U.S. to close what some policymakers called a loophole.
As global AI usage grows, Alibaba has been expanding its capabilities across chips, cloud infrastructure and AI models. It launched its flagship Qwen4-Max AI model earlier this week. In September, Alibaba's CEO called its new Zhenwu V900 chip the “most powerful” AI chip in China, while it announced massive data center investment plans in China and abroad.
Alibaba Cloud’s AI-related revenue currently comes significantly from China and there’s still a lot of “untapped demand” from Chinese enterprises, said Jacob Cooke of the Beijing-based consultancy WPIC Marketing + Technologies.
For the latest July-September quarter, Alibaba reported a 53% year-on-year revenue surge for its AI cloud and compute services to nearly 61 billion yuan ($9 billion). Total revenue for the quarter rose 10% from the year before to almost 272 billion yuan ($41 billion), slightly better than what analysts had expected.
While the company has a strong cash buffer, capital expenditures jumped 60% during the quarter to 50.5 billion yuan ($7.6 billion) thanks to its increased spending on AI infrastructure buildout.
Tencent says US chip curb ‘sets everyone back in China’
Chinese tech giant Tencent on Wednesday said the new U.S. rule on chip access “sets everyone back in China.”
“Everyone is actually having less compute, advanced compute, to work with, no matter when you actually started leasing or building capacities outside of China,” Tencent President Martin Lau said on an earnings call. Training timelines for Tencent’s next versions of its AI models would probably be impacted, he said.
“Chinese AI firms are still heavily dependent on the most frontier Nvidia chips," said James Chai, a researcher at the ISEAS – Yusof Ishak Institute in Singapore, with new U.S. rules on remote access cutting off a huge portion of Chinese firms’ access to compute.
A study released in October by the Institute for Progress, a U.S. think tank, estimated that remote access to AI chips through overseas data centers could account for roughly one-third of China’s AI compute by the end of 2027.
Nvidia, meanwhile, said it is now “no longer shipping” chips including the H200, one of its more powerful chips, though not the most advanced, although the Trump administration greenlighted some sales to China, reflecting how Nvidia has toughened its stance on China following Huang’s ouster.
Analysts expect the U.S. will step up its chip export control policies against China after Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a former senior executive of Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed, raised U.S. national security concerns. Earlier reporting by The New York Times suggested that U.S. officials suspected Alice Huang was a Chinese spy recruited in part to potentially influence Nvidia to make its most advanced chips more available to Chinese companies.
Beijing has rejected claims that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy, and has called the new U.S. rules blocking Chinese companies' remote access to computing power overseas “economic coercion.”
Analysts and industry leaders in China say the U.S.’s tightening of chip export control measures would ultimately accelerate China’s push to make its domestic chip industry self-sufficient.
“Over the longer run, we believe all Chinese players would actually have to rely on domestic supply chains and domestic chips, which we actually see the industry is actually progressing very fast,” said Tencent's Lau.

articles.title_orig: AMD’s China ties complicate its appeal as Nvidia’s rival.
articles.title_zh: AMD’s China ties complicate its appeal as Nvidia’s rival.
articles.content_orig:
Investors and the media hailed AMD as the winner of Nvidia’s China crisis. But AMD firmware keeps turning up at a blacklisted Chinese company and three companies tied to it, just as U.S. export restrictions are scheduled to expand. Is AMD really a safer alternative to Nvidia?
Based on Hunterbrook Media’s reporting, at the time of publication Hunterbrook Capital is short $AMD and long a basket of comparable securities. Positions may change at any time. This article is not investment advice or any recommendation. See full disclosures below.
In March 2025, the U.S. government put IEIT Systems , a Chinese server maker, on its export blacklist.
Over a year and a half later, on October 19, 2026, IEIT posted a software update for one of its AMD servers.
Hunterbrook Media downloaded the file and found AMD’s code inside: the startup firmware that AMD ($AMD) writes for its chips, in a version issued after the blacklisting.
The same firmware is posted on the websites of three other server sellers in AMD’s orbit, none of which are blacklisted. But corporate filings and court records, as well as the software code Hunterbrook reviewed, tie all three to IEIT.
Hunterbrook asked AMD whether it, or any distributor or firmware partner, has provided firmware, technology or support to IEIT since the blacklisting, and under what license. AMD asked for more time and was given until the following day. It said it would be back in touch by then and was not.
A few months ago, investors often looked past stories like these.
Then came Nvidia’s China crisis.
Nvidia ($NVDA) announced that Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive on November 12 amid a scandal that raised national security concerns. Nvidia also faces allegations that billions of dollars worth of its AI chips have reached China through intermediaries in Southeast Asia. Congress is asking how Nvidia’s exports were approved.
AMD has been hailed as one of the biggest winners from Washington to Wall Street. The investment bank William Blair raised its AMD rating partly due to Nvidia’s troubles.
The pitch assumes AMD does not share Nvidia’s problem.
But Hunterbrook’s reporting suggests AMD faces similar risks in China.
The three companies linked to IEIT have been scrutinized before by major outlets, including the New York Times and the Wall Street Journal . But they’ve largely focused on the companies’ ties to Nvidia. Hunterbrook’s reporting suggests AMD may be just as intertwined.
And while the three server vendors linked to IEIT are not currently blacklisted, a U.S. rule scheduled to go into effect in January could close that loophole. Unless its suspension is extended beyond January, the rule will extend export restrictions to foreign companies that are at least 50% owned by blacklisted entities. A separate interim final rule released on the heels of the Nvidia scandal will require licenses for advanced chips shipped to Singapore and four other countries deemed by Commerce as posing a heightened risk of diversion, effective today .
That rule isn’t a one-off reaction to the Nvidia scandal, according to Sam Winter-Levy, a senior fellow at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace. He believes it may signal a “turning point” in U.S. policies on export controls to China.
“The era when you could just sell to whoever you wanted and do whatever you wanted, and the U.S. government didn't really get in the way, I think that's coming to an end,” he added.
AMD’s exposure to this possible policy shift may be larger than Nvidia’s. AMD billed $7.75 billion , or 22.4% of revenue, to China (and Hong Kong) in fiscal 2025, compared to Nvidia’s 9.1% revenue share in those markets. (Though, of course, Nvidia’s revenue tied to these regions may very well be understated!)
Most AMD processors face few export restrictions today. The trouble is that AMD’s growth story rests on the chips that face tighter restrictions. The company has told investors it aims to grow data center AI revenue by more than 80% a year over the next three to five years, chasing a market Nvidia dominates. Those Instinct AI accelerators already need a license to ship to China. When Washington imposed that requirement on AMD’s China-specific MI308 in April 2025, AMD took about $800 million in inventory and related charges.
Breaking News & Investigations. Right to Your Inbox. No Paywalls. No Ads.
IEIT is an arm of Inspur Group, a Chinese company controlled by Shandong province’s state-assets regulator. The Commerce Department added Inspur to its Entity List in March 2023, two years before adding IEIT, saying the companies had tried to acquire U.S. technology for the Chinese military.
AMD writes code that helps prepare its processors and other hardware to run. Server makers incorporate that code into their own BIOS , the firmware that enables the server to run the processors. AMD releases updates, including security fixes , for manufacturers to include in their own BIOS updates.
IEIT’s own release notes show the updates kept coming.
Since the blacklisting, it has incorporated at least six newer versions of AMD’s firmware into updates for three server models. Where AMD’s release dates were public, IEIT’s builds followed about one to two months later. One update posted in October 2025 included a fix for a flaw AMD did not publicly disclose until February 24, 2026.
This is important because Washington treats software updates as exports. William Reinsch — former undersecretary of commerce for export administration and now a senior adviser at the think tank Center for Strategic and International Studies — told Hunterbrook that unlicensed software and hardware transfers are of equal concern.
“The problem is that it's a lot harder to enforce software transfers than it is hardware transfers.”
Reinsch also said not to rule out the possibility AMD had obtained a license to export to IEIT, though the Commerce Department keeps that information from the public. “The fact that you have to get a license does not mean automatically that the license will be denied,” he said, adding that while many companies self-select out of applying in the first place, obtaining one may not be as rare as people think. AMD did not answer repeated questions from Hunterbrook about whether it holds licenses to sell to IEIT.
Enforcement action on illegal software transfers is not without precedent. In October, the Commerce Department settled with Lambda Research, a Massachusetts software company that had sold licenses to China’s SiCarrier, through a distributor and an intermediary, before SiCarrier was added to the Entity List in December 2024. Lambda kept sending automatic updates after the listing. Commerce counted each of the seven updates as a separate violation, even though the software fell in the catch-all category that generally needs no export license. Lambda admitted the conduct.
The fine was small. It was also before the latest crackdown from Commerce on these kinds of arrangements.
Hunterbrook does not know how IEIT obtained AMD’s code, or whether AMD or anyone else held a license to supply it. AMD did not say.
But one route may be through other companies that are not blacklisted and openly sell AMD servers, including companies that records show IEIT may be linked to: China-based Maginfra, Singapore-based Kaytus, and U.S.-based Aivres. IEIT’s code appears across the three server companies.
Hunterbrook compared Maginfra, Aivres , and Kaytus firmware files with IEIT’s firmware and found them to be 99.94% identical to IEIT’s: They are all seemingly for the same AMD server design, which both Aivres and Kaytus sell as the KR2280-E3.
Public benchmark filings point the same way. In a filing published in January 2025, the AMD server Kaytus markets as the KR2280V3 identifies itself as a “KR2280-E3-A0-R0-00,” the model number on Aivres’s datasheet . articles.title_orig: Vladimir Putin invites European leaders to Moscow
articles.title_zh: Vladimir Putin invites European leaders to Moscow
articles.content_orig:
BRUSSELS ― After the EU and its allies wrestled over who should represent them in talks over Ukraine, they now face an even harder decision: play hardball with Russia or try a subtler approach?
The challenge of agreeing on red lines, or principles, for the European team in any negotiations is already proving divisive, with the EU’s chief diplomat Kaja Kallas saying the Europeans should start by demanding as much as possible, and some governments, such as Austria, advocating a looser approach, including confidence-building measures.
“There’s a range of things that Europe should make clear that it’s not ready to discuss,” Norway’s Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide said.
Europe was largely left out of talks between Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. in Abu Dhabi last week, but the Kremlin and the White House signaled that wouldn’t be the case at future meetings. After days of disagreement, EU leaders settled on a team made up of officials from four major countries ― France, Germany, Italy and Poland ― plus the U.K. and top representatives from NATO and the European Commission and Council.
Now, “the focus must shift from the ‘who’ to the ‘what’,” Austrian Foreign Minister Beate Meinl-Reisinger said.
In a 15-point paper shared ahead of a foreign ministers’ meeting on Monday, Austria spelled out what some of those confidence-building measures could be: proposing limited or partial ceasefires to pave the way for a wider truce, for instance, or offering to set up an international forum to monitor any peace agreement.
The proposal amounts to “an offer to all 27 [EU countries] to work towards a common position,” Meinl-Reisinger said.
Norway, which isn’t part of Europe’s negotiating team but had direct contacts with Russia, is also floating ideas to lower tensions. Ukraine’s backers should look back to the Cold War for examples of how Russia and the West managed extreme tensions, specifically the 1975 “Helsinki Accords” which laid out principles for state-to-state relations, Foreign Minister Barth Eide said.
“NATO deployments in NATO countries, for instance, is not a question to discuss with Russia” but Cold War deals on arms limitation “must be relevant in the post-war scenario.”
In the same vein, officials close to the talks are calling for a “flexible” mandate that would allow participants to actually negotiate, rather than have their hands tied. The job of drafting the mandate must go to EU ambassadors in their Coreper meetings, not foreign ministers, argued two EU officials.
Further complicating the matter, such a mandate would bind the European representatives at the table ― the Commission’s Bjoern Seibert, the European Council’s Anna-Maria Boura and the advisers from France, Poland, Italy and Germany ― but not those from the U.K. or NATO.
For Kallas, however, it should be the foreign ministers she gathers in Brussels each month who draft the mandate — and as far as she’s concerned, the approach should demand up-front concessions from Russia rather than the other way around.
“The foreign ministers are ready to take this work forward,” she told reporters on Monday, pointing out that she had already suggested a list of demands .
“I was a lawyer,” she said. “How do you enter negotiations? First, you present or prepare the absolute maximum you want to see. Then, not openly, you also prepare where you are ready to … step back to and what are your red lines, which are absolute no-gos.”
Ministers from several Baltic, Nordic and eastern flank countries echoed Kallas’s approach.
“We have to really keep sequencing, and it means that we have to agree on the ceasefire and when the guns go silent, then we negotiate on the long-lasting peace on Ukraine,” Lithuanian Foreign Minister Kęstutis Budrys said.
Estonia’s chief envoy, Margus Tsahkna, echoed the point: “First, Putin can start the ceasefire. Then negotiations between Russia and Ukraine about peace, and if the peace is there, we need to discuss what kind of security guarantees will be given to Ukraine. We also need Ukrainian security guarantees to our region.”
The only problem is that Europe has already effectively conceded that talks will continue even without a ceasefire. EU negotiators see talks resuming in the coming weeks in Abu Dhabi and are banking on being in the room with Russia’s representatives, according to two EU officials, despite the fact that Moscow is carrying out daily attacks across Ukraine.
“It’s about being pragmatic,” said a senior EU official, granted anonymity to speak frankly. “The people in the room must be able to make decisions.”

articles.content_orig:

White House reporters traveling aboard Air Force One had their phones temporarily confiscated before President Donald Trump’s plane took off after his trilateral summit with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, raising the specter of an unscheduled detour on his way back to Washington D.C.
U.S. officials collected reporters’ devices as the president’s plane prepared to leave Shenzhen, China, Thursday evening.
“At 6:45 pm consider this your wheels up,” the White House pool report read. “Our phones are being taken away for now for security reasons.”
No one on the trip has provided more information. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for more information.
It is highly unusual for reporters’ phones to be sequestered outside of situations when the president is traveling to a war zone, such as when Trump flew to Al Asad Air Base in Iraq at Christmas in 2018, and to Bagram Air Field in Afghanistan for Thanksgiving in 2019.
Fox News correspondent Jacqui Heinrich, the current president of the White House Correspondents’ Association, pointed out on X that the pool’s phones were not taken when Trump left Beijing after his state visit in May.
Separately, a flight restriction that had been imposed over Alaska around the time Air Force One had been scheduled to refuel there was lifted Thursday, raising questions as to the plane’s destination.
The most obvious candidate for a detour is North Korea. Trump spent the days before the summit musing that Kim Jong Un might join him when he met with China ’s Xi and Russia ’s Putin on the sidelines of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation summit.
On Wednesday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters in Manila that the president was “prepared” to meet the North Korean leader.
“It may not happen, but he’s prepared to do it,” Rubio said.
However on a call with reporters before the trip, senior U.S. officials said there were “no plans at all for engagement with North Korea.”
Trump relished the pageantry and attention that were lavished on his first two meetings with Kim, though neither sit-down resulted in the denuclearization deals he had promised to reach with the brutal autocrat.
He also met Kim for a third time during a visit to the Korean Demilitarized Zone and briefly became the first American president to set foot in North Korea.
The intrigue surrounding the president’s departure from China followed Trump’s participation in the first-ever meeting between an American president and the autocrats who have led the other two major nuclear powers for a combined 41 years.
Trump gave Putin a warm reception when he met with him for a bilateral meeting immediately preceding the three-way sit-down.
The U.S. president pointed, smiled and called out “Who is that? He’s my friend!” as he walked into a room with his Russian counterpart. The scene was captured by TV cameras that had been permitted in, even as journalists were barred from attending to prevent the leaders from being asked any uncomfortable questions, though a Russian official attributed the move to space constraints.
Trump said of Putin: “We’ve had a great relationship for many years. We know each other for a long time, and I think a lot of wonderful things can come out of this, or at least start. But I think they’ll come out of this.”
The Kremlin said after the meeting that the pair had discussed the ongoing war in Ukraine , and that Putin left in an “excellent” mood.
The White House offered no official readout of the sit-down, which lasted approximately 40 minutes.
Following the trilateral meeting, the Russian, Chinese and American governments released a four-point “peace declaration” reaffirming that a nuclear war should never be fought and vowing to engage in dialogue on reducing nuclear risks.
The three leaders also pledged to advance reforms of the United Nations, to increase supplies of refined petroleum products for all countries and to uphold the immunity enjoyed by state officials in international courts.
The International Criminal Court in The Hague has issued arrest warrants for Putin and five other Russian officials. The Trump administration has been working to delegitimize and defund the ICC out of fear that Trump and his associates could be subject to war crimes charges over America’s campaign of airstrikes against alleged drug smugglers or an airstrike against an Iranian school that left over 100 children dead.

articles.title_orig: Ukraine strikes Putin’s prized Crimean Bridge for third time in a week
articles.title_zh: Ukraine strikes Putin’s prized Crimean Bridge for third time in a week
articles.content_orig:
Ukraine struck the bridge linking Russia and Crimea for the third time in a week, forcing a suspension of train services across it, Russian authorities said, hours before President Vladimir Putin met the leaders of China and the U.S.
The timing and impact of Ukraine‘s attacks on the bridge, the longest in Europe and a symbol of Putin’s Russia, are awkward for the Kremlin chief as he participates in what Moscow has cast as a historic trilateral summit with President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping .
Moscow hopes the meeting will send a signal to allies and foes that it — rather than the European Union and Britain — is part of an emerging new multilateral world order.
There was no immediate comment on the latest attack from Ukraine or Volodymyr Zelenskyy , its president, who was due to hold talks in Berlin later on Thursday with U.S. peace envoys.
Sergei Aksyonov, Crimea’s Russian-installed governor, issued a defiant video message in which he said rail travel across the bridge would resume later on Thursday.
“We have the strength, the resolve and the understanding of how to resolve this situation. We will overcome everything. Crimea is with Russia forever!” Aksyonov said.
In a statement, Russia’s transport ministry said that nobody had been hurt in the latest Ukrainian attack on the Black Sea peninsula, which Moscow annexed from Ukraine in 2014 , and that specialists were assessing damage to the bridge.
The 12-mile bridge is a flagship project that Putin inaugurated in 2018 and that symbolizes Russia’s attachment to the peninsula, which is also the home of its Black Sea Fleet, whose ships Ukraine has repeatedly targeted.
On Tuesday, Ukrainian drones and missiles destroyed the central road section of the Crimean Bridge, forcing its main road arch to crumble into the sea while leaving a yawning gap, according to videos and images verified by Reuters, dealing a military and symbolic blow to Russia.
That attack is likely to make it harder for Russia to keep up supplies to the peninsula, which is home to nearly 2.5 million people, and is likely to put pressure on Russian military logistics in parts of southern Ukraine held by Moscow’s forces.
This week‘s first attack, on Monday, caused more minor damage to the bridge.

GTA 6 rewards players with extra cash early in the game by investigating some ‘Strange Noises in the Liquor Store’ and interacting with a talking parrot, but finding key locations, including Shirley’s house, isn’t obvious.
Rockstar has made GTA 6 the most open and free game they have ever built, which means a lot of your actions can have consequences. At the same time, it’s a living, breathing open world, with so much happening at every corner, so it’s always great to have an eye out for some kind of unique occurrence, and trust me, there are many .
This GTA 6 guide will explain one such occurrence, which triggers through a different open-world event: Interacting with Jason’s neighbor, Shirley, and eventually finding a talking parrot.
You can buy Grand Theft Auto 6 here if you haven’t already!
Shirley’s house is located just down the road from Jason’s safehouse in GTA 6.
While heading to your safehouse as Jason, you will come across a neighbor named Shirley in the house in the same lane as yours—check out the screenshot below to find the exact location of Shirley’s house.
Shirley asks Jason to buy Salt Squid Rum from a nearby liquor store and bring it back to her. While completing this favor in GTA 6, Jason discovers strange noises in the liquor store: lots of parrot sounds, hinting that it could be an exotic-animal front.
You must eliminate the enemies guarding the talking parrot in GTA 6, behind the liquor store, and locate the cash stash to complete Strange Noises in GTA 6.
Once you’ve given the Salt Squid Rum to Shirley, take some time to explore the game for a few hours. A yellow icon will appear at the same liquor store, signaling that it’s time to investigate (refer to the screenshot below for the exact location).
When you arrive, you’ll find several enemies guarding the area. You have multiple options for how to approach the situation: you can take them down stealthily one by one, challenge them all to fistfights (which is what I chose to do), or go in guns blazing; after all, it is GTA!
As you approach the location, you’ll notice a parrot conversing with the enemies. The parrot even comments on the fistfight happening there. Players can interact with the parrot, and he will reveal the location of a secret cash stash located behind the generator. The generator is on the left side of the building, near the parrot. Behind the generator, there is a vent that contains $1200 in cash.
In this location, there are additional funds and resources available. You can break into the back of the liquor store, access a safe, and collect some petty cash that might be lying around. Overall, it’s possible to grab nearly $2,500 from this place, along with some adrenaline shots and drugs, which provides a significant cash boost in the early game.

articles.title_orig: Pebble Index 01 AI Ring Review: When A Single Feature Becomes The Product
articles.title_zh: Pebble Index 01 AI Ring Review: When A Single Feature Becomes The Product
articles.content_orig:
It’s a whimsical side project for the smartwatch company, but a useful one.
In 2009, Apple CEO Steve Jobs met with the founders of Dropbox with the intention of buying the file-sharing service. As part of the negotiation, Jobs reportedly said Dropbox was a "feature, not a product," and the business couldn't survive long term in its own right. That was my first thought when Pebble CEO Eric Migicovsky showed me the Index 01 back in January. A $75 non-smart ring that puts a tiny microphone on your finger just for speaking to your AI!? Surely, that's a (software) feature on a watch or smart ring, not a whole product you could sell in its own right. All I can say is that I'm glad I didn't say those words out loud at the time, because I'd be eating them today.
The Index 01 is the first of what Migicovsky hopes will be many small, slightly whimsical side projects made by the revived Pebble. It's a non-smart, stainless steel ring which sits on your index finger with a single physical rubber-clad button and an RGB LED.
Inside, you'll find a short range microphone, Bluetooth and a non-rechargeable silver oxide battery. As the rings are sold for $75, and it's designed to be used in tiny bursts, that cell is expected to last between two and three years. When the battery is close to running out, you'll get a ping from Pebble asking if you want to buy a replacement. At that point, you'll also be asked to send back your existing ring for recycling, since Pebble doesn't want to be making more e-waste. A gold star for everyone who can spot the contradiction there.
You'll be able to pick up the Index 01 in US sizes 6-13, and there's a waitlist where you can sign up if you want one in sizes 14 or 15. Pebble says that it's water resistant to one meter, withstanding handwashing, showers and doing the dishes, but it's best not to swim with it.
If you don't know your ring size and don't feel like taking a risk, you can grab a sizing kit from the company. You'll get an injection-molded set of sizers back for you to wear for a day or two to check the fit, and I'd urge you to keep a craft knife or pair of sprue cutters on hand.
As I said, the idea here is to put a physical talk to your device button on your index finger for the thoughts you just need to dump out of your mental cache. By default, if you hold the button and talk, your words will be sent to its homegrown AI, Index Agent, but you can also set it to be processed locally. The button has a wonderfully satisfying click, which is both great to feel and means there's so much resistance that I've only accidentally activated it once in my time wearing it. When active, you need to hold the ring less than a foot away from your mouth to issue your edict (any further is probably physically impossible anyway), and within about 10 seconds it'll be processed on your phone.
Plenty of the things that the Index 01 is doing is the sort of bread-and-butter ambient computing that's been knocking around for years. With your voice, you can leave yourself notes and reminders, add items to a shopping list or set timers, with the system working out where to place each one. There are separate panes inside the Pebble app for Notes to Self, Reminders and Shopping List, which has worked flawlessly so far, even with oblique requests.
You can, of course, also ask Index Agent to answer questions about your schedule and to pull information from the internet. I found the former to be much more reliable than the latter, and the agent managed to embarrass itself in at least one of my tests. One of my usual go-tos is to ask agents who the current manager of a soccer team is, given the volatility of such a role. During testing, Mauricio Pochettino stepped down as the manager of the US men's national team to take over a team sitting in the bottom three of the Premier League. When I asked Index who was running the US men's team, it suggested Pochettino — no great shame in not being that up to date. But, when I asked who was managing the club he was about to take over, it said Ruben Amorim, who was fired January 5, 2026 and has had two successors since then.
Now, I'm the sort of person who doesn't use ambient computing because, for me, I don't like the privacy implications of having a device which is always listening. Equally important, I know I can do whatever task I need with my fingers faster than I could render it as speech. I can set a kitchen timer on my phone in about five seconds, saying it out loud takes twice as long. But the fact Index 01 is only listening when I activate it, and that it's on my finger already, flips the script.
Inside the Pebble app, you can change the destination to whatever AI agent you use, and also change what the trigger action. So, for instance, if you'd rather trigger a web search or a webhook, you can do that, as well as hook up to an MCP server. As I said when reviewing the Pebble Time 2 , the app lacks polish, as the focus is on adding functionality over gloss. And I think the target market — people who didn't just have to look up what a webhook / MCP server was — won't be deterred.
Pebble is an Android-first company, and the ring can do several more things when paired with that ecosystem over iOS. Double click the ring and you'll trigger music playback, a triple click advances to the next song and you can set the ring to send messages via Beeper.
As usual, Pebble has made the point that there are plenty of other devices available if you want something outside its narrow offering. In its materials, the company says if you want a smart ring get an Oura ($399) and if you want a long-term AI recorder, get a Plaud. (The Plaud NotePin is $159, which can continuously record up to 20 hours of audio for later transcription.)
In terms of similar devices, the most obvious choice is the Wizpr Ring , which I saw at CES 2024 when it was called the Whsp Ring . The company is currently fulfilling Indiegogo orders, where rings were priced at $139, but says its retail price will be $199 when it launches. Vocci's ring will set you back $299, can record up to eight hours of conversations at a time and will let you speak to your AI agents. Just bear in mind, it comes with a monthly subscription which will only offer up unlimited transcription at the $30 a month tier. Another option is Aina's far fancier ring , which was announced at the start of November and will ship early next year for $399.
The Pebble Index 01 is nothing more than a physical manifestation of what would otherwise be a software feature. A discrete, standalone button that I'd argue nobody really needs , but it's useful enough to easily justify if you want one. I'm not going to try and dissuade you if your initial reaction was much like mine, because it's the sane and sensible thing to think. But bear in mind that, at this sort of price, it's the type of low-investment gadget that might wind up finding itself an integral part of far more people's days than anyone expects.

articles.title_orig: Thanksgiving dinner will come with higher price tag: Research
articles.title_zh: Thanksgiving dinner will come with higher price tag: Research
articles.content_orig:
This is read by an automated voice. Please report any issues or inconsistencies here .
Record turkey prices and higher fuel costs could make Thanksgiving dinner more expensive this year, according to a survey released Wednesday.
The American Farm Bureau Federation said the cost of an average Thanksgiving feast for 10 will rise 6% from last year to $58.63. The group tracks grocery prices using hundreds of volunteers in all 50 states and Puerto Rico.
The Farm Bureau, which has been tracking Thanksgiving costs for 40 years, said it’s the first time since 2022 that Americans will see the price of the meal increase. The price hit a record of $64.05 in 2022.
High diesel prices have made it more expensive for farmers to process and transport Thanksgiving staples like milk, dinner rolls, potatoes and cranberries, the Farm Bureau said. Diesel prices have surged since the start of the Iran war and hit a record average of $6.53 per gallon in the U.S. in September, according to AAA.
On Wednesday diesel averaged $5.96 per gallon, up 58% from a year ago, AAA said.
Turkey prices have also risen sharply over the past year. The Farm Bureau said the 16-pound turkey in its survey cost an average of $23.68 this year, up from $21.50 last year.
Bird flu has been decimating U.S. turkey flocks since an outbreak began in 2022. But cases have been waning, and turkey production increased substantially this year, said Mark Jordan, the executive director of Leap Market Analytics.
At the same time, turkey demand has been rising, as more Americans seek out lean protein and U.S. turkey exports rise. That strong demand has limited U.S. turkey inventories and raised prices. The U.S. Department of Agriculture expects the wholesale price of a whole frozen turkey hen will average a record $1.76 per pound this year, up 29% from last year.
“Over the last few years there’s been a lot of doom and gloom for the turkey industry,” Jordan said. “This is one of those years that turkey producers are feeling a little bit better about their lot in life.”
Jordan said diesel costs likely didn’t impact turkey prices this year, since so much of the decision-making and timing related to the turkeys that will be consumed this Thanksgiving happened before diesel prices spiraled. But diesel costs could have a notable impact on turkey prices next year, he said.
A few of the items on the Thanksgiving menu are cheaper than last year, the Farm Bureau said. A 1-pound vegetable tray featuring carrots and celery is 5 cents cheaper, while a 16-ounce bag of frozen peas is 4 cents cheaper. Frozen pie crusts are also slightly cheaper, although a can of pumpkin pie filling is more expensive.
And in some cases, stores will price turkey and other Thanksgiving staples lower in order to draw shoppers. Aldi said its feast for 10, which mirrors the Farm Bureau’s menu, costs $39 this year. Walmart, which adds items like corn muffin mix and marshmallows but doesn’t include carrots and celery, said its feast for 10 is $35.
Persistently high grocery prices have been frustrating Americans since the pandemic and played a role in Republicans’ recent losses in the midterm elections. Prices for food eaten at home jumped 22% between October 2021 and October 2026, according to U.S. government data. That’s almost double the usual pace of food price inflation.
This year, the USDA predicts prices for food eaten at home to rise 2.3%. That would be lower than the recent annual average of 2.6%.
Durbin writes for the Associated Press.

articles.title_orig: U.S. Jobless Claims Unexpectedly Move Higher
articles.title_zh: U.S. Jobless Claims Unexpectedly Move Higher
articles.content_orig:
This is read by an automated voice. Please report any issues or inconsistencies here .
Slightly more people applied for U.S. unemployment benefits last week, though layoffs remain low and most American workers enjoy solid job security.
The Labor Department said Thursday that jobless claims ticked up to 203,000 from a revised 202,000 the week before. The four-week average of claims, which smooths out week-to-week volatility, rose 2,000 to 197,750.
Applications for unemployment aid are a proxy for layoffs, and economists watch them because they can be a sign of where the job market is headed. This year, claims have remained at a historically low level below 220,000.
The report suggests that most companies are confident enough in the economy and their sales to hold onto their workers. At the same time, hiring has been sluggish, resulting in a “low-hire, low-fire” job market.
Even so, job creation has improved in the past few months. Employers added 165,000 jobs in October, far more than economists forecast, while the unemployment rate ticked down to 4.1%, from 4.2%.
The U.S. economy is expanding at a solid pace as consumer spending has remained resilient despite elevated inflation, which has eroded Americans’ inflation-adjusted earnings. Investment in data centers is also powering the economy.
Yet the growth has spurred only limited hiring. Many economists are watching job data closely to evaluate whether artificial intelligence is displacing workers, but so far it hasn’t led to a pickup in layoffs. Some companies may be delaying hiring as they implement the technology.
The economy grew at a 3.4% annual rate in the July-September quarter, up from just 2.2% in the previous three months. The Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta forecasts that it will expand at a similarly healthy 3.2% pace in the final three months of the year.
Rugaber writes for the Associated Press.

articles.title_orig: Stocks making the biggest moves Thursday: Palo Alto Networks, Take-Two Interactive, Everpure, Walmart & more
articles.title_zh: Stocks making the biggest moves Thursday: Palo Alto Networks, Take-Two Interactive, Everpure, Walmart & more
articles.content_orig:
Palo Alto Networks popped in early trading Thursday, boosted by quarterly results that beat analyst expectations. AMD, meanwhile, tumbled on the back of a short seller report.
Follow along as CNBC covers the biggest stock market moves of the day.
Neocloud CoreWeave gained 1% on enthusiasm from the Anthropic IPO plus a change in Texas permitting that favors data center development.
Texas officials started issuing air permits again for data center construction projects, according to Reuters , which bodes well for the future of the physical component of the AI buildout.
Nvidia's highly anticipated earnings call earlier this week also offered clarity on the leadership direction for the firm, which Wall Street analysts responded positively to. Analysts at Truist were encouraged on Tuesday by Nvidia statements on the call about its relationship to neoclouds.
"Notably, NVIDIA's earnings commentary … [described] neoclouds as an 'increasingly important' part of the global AI infrastructure ecosystem and stating that it will continue working with and supporting leading neocloud partners, while becoming more disciplined and selective in that support."
AMD shares tumbled more than 9% after Hunterbrook Capital revealed it took a short position on the company.
In a post titled "AMD has its own China problem", Hunterbrook alleges that "AMD firmware keeps turning up at a blacklisted Chinese company and three companies tied to it, just as U.S. export restrictions are scheduled to expand."
"AMD, which bills over 20% of its revenue to customers in China and Hong Kong, also depends on a Chinese partner to finish most of its chips," Hunterbrook added.
CNBC reached out to AMD for comment.
Shares of Coherent are up nearly 11%, extending gains after Nvidia 's latest earnings report earlier in the week highlighted continued demand for data-center technology.
Coherent, which supplies optical components used in AI data centers, said its data-center revenue rose 85% year over year in its fiscal first quarter.
On Nov. 18, the company's board authorized a share repurchase program of up to $2 billion . Coherent may buy shares in the open market or through other transactions. The program has no expiration date and does not require the company to repurchase a specific amount.
Shares of the software company making tools for computer chips jumped 3.2% after Barclays initiated coverage with an overweight rating and a $640 price target implying 47% upside from Wednesday's close. Analyst Saket Kalia noted that Synopsys is the leader of a growing Electronic Design Automation (EDA) market, which is driven by rising spend in semiconductor research and development.
MongoDB gained 4% before the bell following an upgrade at UBS to buy from neutral.
The bank's channel checks pointed to steady demand and better-than-expected consumer and partner growth, which should support durable 20%-plus total revenue growth and 25%-plus revenue growth for its cloud database service Atlas over the coming years, analyst Radi Sultan said.
In addition, MongoDB could be utilized in 20% to 40% of incremental AI workloads, which is not fully reflected in the stock's valuation, he said.
Data storage stocks are getting a lift in the premarket Thursday as the Anthropic IPO aims to breathe new life into AI-trade
Shares of Seagate Technology are up more than 6% while Western Digital stock popped 5.8%.
Seagate and Western Digital provide provide mass data storage infrastructure, a crucial role in the AI ecosystem to help AI models run.
The strong momentum around data storage and AI infrastructure demand is already high.
But a large chuck of that demand will come from leading AI lab Anthropic, which is set to go public Thursday.
Chipmakers advanced on Thursday ahead of Anthropic's IPO.
Marvell gained 4.2%, Advanced Micro Devices is up 2.8%, Broadcom advanced 2.5%, Intel moved 4.4% higher and Nvidia is up 1.5%.
These artificial intelligence chips will help Anthropic run Claude models faster.
Leading chipmakers need the IPO to go well, as Anthropic has $900 billion in spending commitments.
Shares of Bloom Energy surged nearly 8% in the premarket Thursday after being upgraded to outperform at BMO Capital Markets.
The analysts cited their endorsement of the company after coming away with positive meetings with management.
The firm however decreased its price target to $230 from $260, which still implies a 35% upside to the stock's Thursday close of $170 per share.
UBS upgraded the intelligent content management provider to buy from neutral, sending shares 3.6% higher in premarket trading.
The firm believes Box 's recent artificial intelligence growth acceleration can support sustained double-digit revenue growth. "Investors have been looking for evidence that AI can drive an inflection in software growth, and Box is increasingly demonstrating exactly that," analyst Taylor McGinnis wrote.
Walmart shares were down more than 1% even after the retail giant reported third-quarter results that beat expectations and raised its full-year guidance.
The company posted adjusted earnings per share of 65 cents on revenue of $188.84 billion. Analysts expected a profit of 64 cents per share on revenue of $187.27 billion.
For the year, Walmart sees net sales rising 4.9% to 5.2%, more than a previous guidance of 4% to 5%.
Shares of Take-Two Interactive slipped 1%, giving back some of their gains from the previous session. The stock popped more than 6% on Wednesday ahead of the release of the much-anticipated "Grand Theft Auto VI" game.
Take-Two is up nearly 14% in November, though the stock has dropped 15% in 2026.
Cybersecurity player Palo Alto Networks advanced 10% after its fiscal first-quarter results came in above the Street's expectations.
The company earned $1.05 per share on an adjusted basis and revenue of $3.44 billion. The LSEG consensus estimate called for 97 cents per share on $3.31 billion of revenue.
Guidance for the fiscal year ending July 2027 calls for adjusted earnings of $4.26 to $4.30 per share on revenue of $14.52 billion to $14.57 billion. Analysts sought $4.18 per share and $14.16 billion, according to LSEG.
The data management company advanced 5% after raising its guidance for the fiscal-year ending January 2027.
Everpure sees revenue in a range of $5.20 billion to $5.21 billion, up from its earlier call of $5.03 billion to $5.07 billion. Analysts polled by FactSet were looking for $5.06 billion.
Third-quarter results also surpassed estimates on the top and bottom lines.
The manufacturer of power generation equipment pulled back 1%. Woodward expects adjusted earnings for the fiscal year ending September 2027 to range between $10.20 and $10.70 per share, below the FactSet consensus estimate of $10.74 per share.

articles.title_zh: Major KFC franchisee files for bankruptcy, puts 84 restaurants up for sale
articles.content_orig:
This is read by an automated voice. Please report any issues or inconsistencies here .
See more from the L.A. Times in Google Search. Set us as preferred
A San Diego-based franchisee of Outback Steakhouse filed for bankruptcy on Monday, citing expensive food and labor costs and declining customer traffic.
Cerca Trova Restaurant Group, which operates 61 Outback Steakhouse locations mostly in California, said it has been struggling since the COVID-19 pandemic . The company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Wilmington, Del., seeking relief from hundreds of millions in debt.
Cerca Trova also operates Outback Steakhouses in Arizona, Colorado, Nevada and New Mexico but said that California’s minimum wage laws have made labor especially pricey for a majority of its restaurants.
More than half the company’s employees work in California, according to court documents.
California’s minimum wage, effective at the start of this year, is $16.90 per hour. Fast-food employers must pay a higher minimum wage of $20 per hour, but Outback Steakhouse is not classified as a fast-food establishment under the law.
Beverly Hills-based Fat Brands Inc. said in a statement that it filed for bankruptcy on Monday to restructure the debt it accumulated while expanding its company portfolio, citing ‘difficult and largely unforeseen’ market conditions.
“By 2026, the pressures on the business had converged,” Cerca Trova Chief Executive David Goronkin said in a court filing. “Guest traffic and earnings continued to decline, while food, labor, and other production costs continued to rise.”
The company’s debt has increased from $269 million in late 2020 to $449 million this year. It has between one and 49 creditors, court documents said.
Outback Steakhouse is not the only full-service casual dining restaurant to face challenges since the pandemic.
Red Lobster filed for bankruptcy in 2024, after its disastrous $20 all-you-can-eat shrimp deal . More recently, the Oprah-backed chain True Food Kitchen filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and closed three Southern California locations.
Inflation and economic pressure have led more Americans to eat at home or turn to fast food for a cheaper option, while the rise of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs such as Ozempic has curbed customers’ appetites.
The cost of beef has also been rising, up as much as 5% each year since 2022, Cerca Trova said in court filings.
Shares of Wendy’s jumped 15% at the opening bell after noted investor Nelson Peltz made an offer to buy the struggling burger chain
Cerca Trova was once the largest Outback Steakhouse franchisee, with 99 restaurants in 2018. As of June, there were 659 Outback Steakhouse locations nationwide, 544 owned and operated by the brand owner, Bloomin’ Brands. The rest are run by franchisees.
Bloomin’ Brands, headquartered in Tampa, Fla., also owns Bonefish Grill, Carrabba’s Italian Grill and Fleming’s Prime Steakhouse and Wine Bar.
The company has thrived this year despite pressures on the restaurant industry, with shares rising 60% since January. Shares fell Tuesday after Cerca Trova’s bankruptcy announcement and ended the day at $10.23, down 6.15%.  The company’s market value is nearly $879 million.
The Scottsdale, Ariz.-based health food chain True Food Kitchen announced it filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on Monday and has closed 12 locations.
Cerca Trova, also known as Out West Restaurant Group, proposed selling its assets to Bloomin’ Brands for $26.3 million unless a higher offer emerges during the bankruptcy process.
“This is an isolated situation involving the franchisee and does not affect Bloomin’ Brands’ corporate operations, financing, or liquidity,” Bloomin’ Brands spokesperson Elizabeth Daly said in an email. “Bloomin’ Brands is participating in the process as a stalking‑horse bidder to acquire Out West’s assets and seeking to support operational continuity and protect the brand while the court‑supervised process moves forward. ”
Cerca Trova could not be immediately reached for comment.

articles.title_orig: In an authoritarian economy, Jensen Huang may be too big to fail | Robert Reich
articles.title_zh: In an authoritarian economy, Jensen Huang may be too big to fail | Robert Reich
articles.content_orig:
A handful of men control the US economy. They have leveraged themselves to be – or seem – indispensable
Jensen Huang has said he would return to Nvidia as its CEO if its board requests it.
“I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said . “If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”
Huang, who admitted being unfaithful to his wife, resigned from Nvidia last week. US intelligence agencies have identified one of his alleged lovers as a spy for China. If true, Nvidia’s most advanced AI chips may have found their way there.
Beyond the tabloid headlines lies a much bigger story – a US economy that’s become dependent on the initiatives and decisions of a few powerful men who are too big to fail.
We tend to think of government as being authoritarian, democratic or somewhere in between. For the last 22 months, we’ve witnessed what happens when the US government turns authoritarian.
An economy can also be described along the same continuum.
Throughout most of the last century, the US economy was fairly democratic. Decisions about what was produced and at what price reflected the judgments of tens of thousands of corporate executives, managers and small-business owners – all of whom were trying to respond to consumers and investors. Through labor unions, workers also had some say.
But the US economy has become far more authoritarian.
In recent decades, it’s become concentrated in the hands of a few giant corporations. Economies of scale have enabled those corporations to spread their fixed costs over many goods and services, and the US government has nearly abandoned antitrust (anti-monopoly) enforcement.
Labor unions have shrunk from representing over a third of private-sector workers in the 1950s to just 6% today.
More recently – over the last five years – something else has occurred, especially in big tech, that’s pushed the economy much further toward authoritarianism.
A handful of men – among them, Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos, Mark Zuckerberg, Larry Ellison, Tim Cook and Jensen Huang – have not only become the richest people in the world, with significant political clout. They also control the direction and pace of technologies on which the US and the world depend.
These men are, in fact, the authoritarians of the new economy. They have unparalleled power over every aspect of the lives of Americans and millions of others around the world. And they have leveraged themselves to be, or seem, too big to fail.
The leverage works like this.
Nvidia’s value depends on Jensen Huang.
Hours after Huang’s resignation last Thursday, Nvidia stock dropped 10.3% in pre-market trading, erasing approximately $490bn of Nvidia’s value by the time the market opened.
Since the start of the leadership controversy at Nvidia on 8 November, the company has lost about $800bn in market value.
The AI industry, in turn, depends on Nvidia. Nvidia controls about 90% of the global market share of advanced AI chips. It has also become the major financier for the entire AI industry. Some call Nvidia the “ central bank of AI ”.
Nvidia’s $5tn market value (before 8 November) equaled about 8% of the total value of the S&P 500.
The US economy, in turn, depends on the AI industry. In the first quarter of 2025, the buildouts of datacenters using Nvidia chips accounted for 92% of US economic growth. Over the past two years, AI has been responsible for roughly half of America’s overall growth.
This huge leverage also works in reverse. Analysts fear that Nvidia’s collapse could cause the AI bubble to burst, triggering a failure that could threaten the entire US, if not also the world, economy.
Most Americans’ 401(k)s are invested in giant index funds tied to the Nasdaq and S&P 500. The Nasdaq and S&P 500, in turn, are based largely on 10 huge corporations . These 10 corporations are all connected to Nvidia. Together, they comprise about 37% of the value of the entire US stock market.
What all this means is Jensen Huang may be too big to fail.
More than 177,000 people have so far signed a “Stand with Jensen” open letter demanding that Nvidia’s board of directors “bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts”. Signers include Elon Musk; the Y Combinator president, Garry Tan; the Epic Games CEO, Tim Sweeney; and thousands of self-reported Nvidia employees.
Huang is discussing a possible return to the company, though the chair of the company’s board has said it’s not considering the move . One Huang ally talks of a “war room” of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for the former Nvidia ‌CEO’s return, ‌and garner support from ‌Trump. “Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen,” the person told the Financial Times, adding that the efforts have Huang’s support.
Trump told reporters on Monday that he “would not mind” if Huang were reinstated as Nvidia CEO, adding that he thought Huang had “learned a big lesson”.
Exactly what “big lesson” did Trump have in mind? That it’s not a good look for the CEO of the US’s most valuable corporation to have a romantic relationship out of wedlock?
Or that such a CEO shouldn’t break the law by supplying America’s most advanced AI chips to China through a Chinese spy?
On Tuesday, it was announced that Huang has agreed to appear on 1 December before the House foreign affairs committee, the select committee on the Chinese Communist party and the House intelligence committee in transcribed interviews.
Even in an authoritarian economy, no CEO is above the law. Or is he? We may soon find out.
Robert Reich, a former US secretary of labor, is a professor of public policy emeritus at the University of California, Berkeley. He is a Guardian US columnist and his newsletter is at robertreich.substack.com . His new book, Coming Up Short: A Memoir of My America, is out now in the US and in the UK

articles.title_orig: Popular cruise ship rocked by illness outbreak as nearly 150 passengers and crew fall victim
articles.title_zh: Popular cruise ship rocked by illness outbreak as nearly 150 passengers and crew fall victim
articles.content_orig:
Infectious disease specialist Dr. Tyler Evans of California discusses the gastrointestinal illness outbreak aboard the Caribbean Princess — and shares tips for how to stay safe.
A Caribbean cruise has taken an uncomfortable turn for nearly 150 passengers and crew members who have fallen sick with stomach illness symptoms — with an infectious disease expert providing important insight into a very "common" issue.
A total of 148 people aboard Princess Cruises' Caribbean Princess — 134 passengers and 14 crew members — have reported the symptoms, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).
The ship departed Nov. 11 and is not scheduled to return until Nov. 23. It is carrying 2,936 passengers and 1,132 crew members, the CDC said.
HIGHLY CONTAGIOUS NOROVIRUS SPREADS ON CRUISE SHIP, SICKENING OVER 100 PASSENGERS AND CREW
Its 12-night round-trip voyage from Fort Lauderdale, Florida, includes scheduled stops in Aruba, Colombia, the Panama Canal, Costa Rica and Grand Cayman , according to the ship's itinerary.
Princess Cruises reported the outbreak to the CDC's Vessel Sanitation Program (VSP) on Nov. 15. It also confirmed the situation in a statement to Fox News Digital.
Nearly 150 passengers and crew members aboard Princess Cruises' Caribbean Princess have fallen ill during a 12-night voyage. The CDC is monitoring the issue. (iStock)
"Princess Cruises can confirm that a limited number of guests aboard Caribbean Princess have reported mild gastrointestinal illness," the company said in its statement.
"Our crew responded promptly by implementing enhanced sanitation protocols across the ship, including comprehensive cleaning and disinfection measures ."
It concluded, "While most guests remain unaffected, we are continuing to closely monitor the situation."
Test results are still pending, and the CDC said it is monitoring the ship's cleaning efforts and response.
Those affected have experienced vomiting and diarrhea, though health officials have not yet determined what caused the illness .
In response, the CDC said the cruise line and crew have taken several steps to limit the spread of illness on board.
CRUISE BUFFET GUESTS FACE SURPRISE CHARGES FOR TAKING FOOD BACK TO CABINS
Those steps include more frequent cleaning and disinfecting, keeping sick passengers and crew members away from others, and working with health officials on cleaning procedures and reporting cases.
Crew members also collected stool samples from sick individuals to help identify the cause of the outbreak, the agency said.
A percentage of passengers and crew members aboard the Caribbean Princess have reported vomiting and diarrhea, though the cause of the outbreak as of now is unknown. (iStock)
Test results are still pending, and the CDC said it is monitoring the ship's cleaning efforts and response.
Fox News Digital reached out to the CDC for further details.
Health officials say it can take time to figure out what is making people sick on a cruise ship. While norovirus is a common cause of stomach illnesses on cruise ships, the CDC said it is not always clear what is causing an outbreak when it's first reported.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES
The agency also noted that the 148 cases of illness were reported over the course of the trip so far — so not everyone became sick at the same time.
To help prevent stomach illnesses, the CDC recommends washing hands often, especially after using the bathroom and before eating .
Crew members aboard the ship have increased cleaning and disinfection efforts to help limit the spread of illness during the cruise. (Alfredo Martinez/Getty Images)
"This is not the first time we've seen this with cruise ships," said Dr. Tyler Evans, an adult infectious diseases and addiction medicine physician who is also CEO, founder and chief medical officer for Wellness Equity Alliance in California.
"Cruise ships, I often say, are sort of floating Petri dishes. They're these massive congregate facilities on the sea."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER
He said gastrointestinal illnesses on ships are "very, very common." A main reason is the food, he said — especially buffet set-ups , he noted.
For anyone connected to this particular incident, he said individuals should look for "any sudden onset of vomiting and watery diarrhea. I know it's not glamorous to talk about," he added, "but if you are on the toilet more than five times a day, that is definitely an indication this is not normal and should be checked out by a primary care provider."
Those with at-risk health conditions, particularly older adults, should be seen very promptly by doctors, a physician said. (iStock)
Those with at-risk health conditions, particularly older adults, should be seen very promptly by doctors, he also said.
Pregnant women as well as children need to be treated urgently as well, he said.
The Caribbean Princess outbreak comes as other cruise ships have also reported similar illnesses this year.
In March, 65 passengers and 11 crew members fell ill aboard Holland America's Westerdam during a February voyage in Asia, Fox News Digital previously reported.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
Those affected reported diarrhea, vomiting and fever. Tests conducted by the ship's lab found that stool samples from seven patients were positive for norovirus.
Health officials in Hong Kong boarded the ship on March 1 to investigate the outbreak.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The cruise line said it increased cleaning and disinfection efforts, while authorities inspected the vessel before allowing new passengers and crew members to board.
Jessica Mekles of Fox News Digital contributed reporting.
Kelly McGreal is a member of the lifestyle team at Fox News Digital. She and the team cover travel, food and drink, health, relationships and more. She also produces the weekly American Culture Quiz and handles other special projects.

articles.title_orig: Feature: 20 Wii Exclusives You Should Track Down While You Still Can
articles.title_zh: Feature: 20 Wii Exclusives You Should Track Down While You Still Can
articles.content_orig:
Somehow, someway, it's been two whole decades since the Revolution began and an elderly relative who had never played a video game in their life somehow, someway, thrashed you at Wii Sports bowling.
The little system that could went on to sell over 100 million units across its lifetime, which means that 20 years on it's still possible to pick up a good clean one for a reasonable price - something which can't be said for a certain autostereoscopic handheld with a divergent family tree.
It also means that secondhand software is still plentiful for the most part, with much of the system's catalogue still available for not-silly money (plus some for silly money). So today we're rounding up 20 gems to consider picking up for your trusty Wii.
Subscribe to Nintendo Life on YouTube 855k
If you're just looking for the Best Wii Games™, we've got you covered elsewhere . Here, we're specifically looking for games slightly off the beaten track, games that were either full-on exclusives or, in a couple of cases where I've stretched the definition, are difficult to find anywhere else.
Ready? Let's dive right into things...
Kicking things off with the Batman, Wayforward's take on the Cartoon Network series captured perfectly the audio-visual elements of the show with a ton of amusing dialogue and a fun, animated take on a character that — outside of his Lego iteration — had gotten pretty dark and self-serious in the movies and other games of the era.
Batman: The Brave and the Bold - The Videogame (or Das Videospiel as my German copy has it) offers simple side-scrolling brawling, but the BAM-BOOM-POW energy is infectious, and this is a great one to play with the kids. There was a DS version, although that's single-player only, so stick with Wii.
Steven Spielberg's making a game, everybody! Legendary Hollywood director Steven Spielberg! The moment we heard that, we imagined Indiana Jones -style derring-do, or something with aliens or dinosaurs. We didn't imagine that the title prominently flagged as "A Steven Spielberg / EA Game" would be a physics-based block puzzler/party game in the Jenga mould.
However, 2008's Boom Blox turned out to be an absolute blast, especially with friends, and a game that made great use of the system's unique controller. it absolutely deserves to be revisited.
A sequel, Boom Blox Bash Party , followed in 2009, and that's a good time, too.
Dead Space: Extraction was a prequel to the 360-era sci-fi/survival horror game PS3/360 game, and perhaps benefited from low expectations, but it's a cracking, moody little rail shooter.
This one came to PS3 two years later with Move controller support, but this rail shooter was built for the Wii and made use of one of the system's best features: the IR camera-powered pointer in the Wiimotes. For accuracy and responsiveness, this fairly low-tech solution to pointer controls still trumps the gyro alternative (which constantly needs resetting/recentring) in our book, and this game is worth setting up the sensor bar.

articles.title_orig: Mrima Hill deal: US consortium wins Kenya mining project, beating Chinese rivals
articles.title_zh: Mrima Hill deal: US consortium wins Kenya mining project, beating Chinese rivals
articles.content_orig:
A US-led consortium, Frontier Minerals, has won the tender to develop Kenya's Mrima Hill mining project, beating seven bidders, including companies from China and Australia.
The site is estimated to hold deposits of critical minerals worth more than $60bn (£45bn), including niobium, used in electric vehicles, aerospace and defence technology.
Frontier Minerals says its proposal aims to keep more of the economic benefits in Kenya through "processing and refining of minerals in-country".
The deal comes as Washington seeks greater access to Africa's minerals, aiming to strengthen US supply chains and compete with China.
Frontier Minerals brings together three US companies - Bunker Hill Mining Corp, American Resources Corporation and ReElement Technologies Corporation. The consortium combines expertise in mineral resource development, critical materials supply chains and advanced refining technologies.
A central part of its proposal is to develop mineral processing and refining capacity in Kenya. Brad Barnett from Frontier Minerals said the company wanted the country to capture more value from its mineral resources.
Mrima Hill is located in Kwale County, near Kenya's Indian Ocean coastline. The site covers about 390 acres of forest.
The prospect of mining in the area has raised concerns among local residents, who fear the project could damage the forest and threaten their ancestral heritage.
There are also questions over whether communities living near the site will benefit from the investment.
Barnett was keen to reassure Kenyans that they would benefit: "We intend to create lasting opportunities for Kenyan workers, businesses and the wider economy through capacity-building and targeted investment, while prioritising environmental management and performance."
The consortium must still obtain a prospecting licence and meet the necessary regulatory requirements before the project can proceed.
The tender decision has drawn objections from competing bidders.
Reuters news agency reports that two rival companies intend to challenge the selection, with Australia's RareX alleging that Frontier Minerals missed an earlier submission deadline.
Kenya's government has maintained that the process was open and transparent.
The project comes as US strives to secure alternative sources of critical minerals and reduce dependence on China, which dominates the processing of several key minerals.
Washington has been pursuing partnerships with mineral-rich African countries, including the Democratic Republic of Congo and Zambia, as it seeks to strengthen supply chains for industries ranging from electric vehicles to defence technology.
Kenya's mining ministry says the sector is an important part of its plans to diversify the economy beyond traditional sources of revenue such as tourism, agriculture and financial services.

articles.title_orig: World Toilet Day is a funny idea with a serious goal: A world awash in toilets
articles.title_zh: World Toilet Day is a funny idea with a serious goal: A world awash in toilets
articles.content_orig:
World Toilet Day 2026 focuses on the connection between sanitation and gender equality. Access to safe, private and dignified toilets is essential to protecting the health and safety of women and girls, supporting their education and livelihoods, and enabling their full participation in society.
Sanitation is foundational to gender equality. By the end of 2025, 82.2 million people were living in internal displacement within their own countries (IDMC, 2026). Many live in camps and informal settlements where sanitation facilities are shared, overcrowded or inadequate. For displaced women and girls, the lack of safe toilets can affect their daily routines, mobility and access to education and livelihood opportunities.
The sanitation crisis affects everyone, but not equally. Unsafe sanitation exposes women and girls to diseases, danger and abuse. In displacement-affected communities, communal toilets without functioning locks, adequate lighting or sex-segregated facilities can compromise privacy and expose women and girls to heightened protection risks, including gender-based violence.
Safe sanitation is a universal human right, and safe toilets mean equal futures. Everyone should have access to sanitation facilities that are safe, accessible, private, inclusive and responsive to their needs. This requires not only appropriate infrastructure, but also meaningful community participation, effective management and regular maintenance.
IOM works to ensure that migrants, displaced populations and host communities have equitable access to safe, dignified and inclusive water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services, recognizing their essential role in protecting health, safety and dignity, particularly in crisis and displacement settings. In 2025, IOM reached 5.1 million people with WASH support across 61 countries and territories, including 1.26 million people with safe sanitation (IOM IQBis, 2025).
IOM designs WASH services with women and girls, including those with disabilities, so that facilities are safe, accessible and meet their menstrual health and hygiene needs. Risks of gender-based violence are identified and mitigated at every stage.

articles.title_orig: Microsoft To Do will soon become Microsoft Done
articles.title_zh: Microsoft To Do will soon become Microsoft Done
articles.content_orig:
Apps retire in June 2027, with no automatic task migration and no Planner replacement for personal accounts
Microsoft has slipped some bad news into this week's Ignite AI puffery: the To Do apps are retiring on June 30, 2027, ending a journey that began with its acquisition of Wunderlist more than a decade ago.
The confirmation came in an announcement about unified tasks and plans for Copilot and Microsoft 365. Until now, there was To Do or Planner (in basic or premium guise). The idea is "a single system for tracking your work as an individual, as a team, and as an organization." To Do contributes features to that future, but its apps don't get to join it.
The problem is that Planner doesn't do everything To Do does. Microsoft would like users to migrate to Planner but, by the company's own admission , there are plenty of gaps. No native Windows or Mac desktop apps are planned to replace To Do; file attachments aren't supported on tasks in the Planner private plan, and there's no equivalent to To Do list groups in Planner. "Equivalent To Do printing and email-list capabilities are not currently planned for the replacement experience," and so on.
Existing To Do tasks and lists won't migrate to Planner either. They'll remain accessible through Planner until June 30, 2027, but that access ends with the apps. Microsoft says the date does not itself trigger deletion of the underlying data.
Personal Microsoft account holders are left in an even worse state: Planner isn't available to them, including Microsoft 365 Personal and Family subscribers. Microsoft's advice is to choose another task-management app and prepare to export their data. Export instructions are still to come, and exporting won't necessarily produce something another app can import.
Very much a case of "don't let the door hit you on the way out."
Unifying tasks and plans is a good idea – the current situation does create confusion, as Microsoft acknowledged. However, taking an axe to To Do, which was developed to be a successor to Wunderlist ( acquired in 2015 for a figure between $100 million and $200 million, an early action under Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella), seems extreme.
Microsoft calls the replacement "a unified platform for people and agents across Microsoft 365" and stated: "This unified platform makes accessing Planner through Copilot, Cowork and Autopilot easier."
Some users responding to the announcement were unimpressed, with one declaring "What a mess," and another asking if To Do might be spun off into an open source project: "Not everything needs to be put into an AI/Copilot agent."
Indeed, it doesn't. But a useful service that doesn't ram Copilot and AI integration down customers' throats at every opportunity? That would never do.
The message for To Do users appears to be: Get with the Plan(ner) or just get out. ®
